title: The 2026 Childhood Immunization Schedule
date_evidence: Report cover dateline 'June 11, 2026' with product number R48982 (congress.gov / everycrsreport R48982.html)
key_claim: The CDC's January 2026 revised childhood immunization schedule uses a three-tier structure (recommended for all children; risk-based; and shared clinical decision-making), changing the recommendation type for Hepatitis A, Meningitis ACWY and RSV to risk-based/SCDM and for rotavirus and influenza to SCDM; because most young children are covered through the Vaccines for Children (VFC) program or private health insurance, the revised schedule has federal policy implications for VFC, ACA private-insurance no-cost coverage requirements, and the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program.
frame_summary: CRS frames the 2026 schedule as a structural change whose main consequences run through the federal coverage programs (VFC, ACA private insurance, VICP) that are pegged to ACIP/CDC recommendations.
notes: Tier-1 non-partisan reference (11 June 2026) for the schedule's three-tier structure and its coverage-program implications. Fetched via everycrsreport mirror; cover dateline 'June 11, 2026 R48982'.

title: Changes to CDC Vaccine Recommendations in 2025 and 2026
date_evidence: Congressional Research Service issued Insight IN12684 on April 28, 2026 (authors Kavya Sekar and Alexandria K. Mickler)
key_claim: HHS changed multiple vaccine recommendations without consulting ACIP, including the entire childhood immunization schedule in January 2026; the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued a stay on March 16, 2026 postponing the effective date of the revised 2026 childhood immunization schedule (reverting to the May 2025 version), the appointments of the 13 ACIP members named in June 2025, and all committee votes after June 11, 2025.
frame_summary: CRS frames the 2026 changes as procedurally irregular and now judicially paused, documenting the March 2026 court stay that reverted the childhood schedule to its May 2025 version.
notes: Tier-1 non-partisan reference (28 April 2026) for the litigation timeline and the March 16 2026 stay. Congress.gov CRS pages render dynamically; date corroborated by the CRS product record and Targeted News Service redistribution.

title: Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP); Notice of Charter Re-establishment
date_evidence: Federal Register document 2026-10012, dated 2026/05/19 (URL path); corroborated by CIDRAP (12/06/2026): 'HHS recently issued a revised charter to re-establish the group'
key_claim: HHS re-established the ACIP charter via a Federal Register notice on 19 May 2026, one of two charter rewrites since the March 2026 court stay, broadening membership-eligibility criteria and the committee's scope of work while ACIP remained without a functioning quorum.
frame_summary: The Federal Register notice frames the charter re-establishment as a routine administrative step, while critics read it as an attempt to re-qualify contested appointees.
notes: Tier-1 primary document (19 May 2026) for the ACIP charter re-establishment. Cited minimally for the charter-rewrite fact and date; corroborated by CIDRAP (12/06/2026) which links the same Federal Register notice, and by Medical Daily (30/06/2026).

title: HHS asks for expedited appeal of court ruling on US vaccine policy
date_evidence: Published 12 June 2026, reporting HHS's same-day filing: 'on June 12, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy announced that the agency had filed a motion asking the First Circuit to expedite their appeal'; article references an AAP statement 'today' and the 19 May revised charter
key_claim: HHS filed a motion to expedite its First Circuit appeal of the March 16, 2026 district-court ruling (Judge Brian Murphy) that blocked the CDC's childhood-schedule changes and froze the reconstituted ACIP; ACIP has not met since December 2025 and cannot issue new recommendations, review newly approved vaccines, or complete work ahead of the fall flu season, and HHS has issued a revised charter to re-establish the group.
frame_summary: CIDRAP frames the appeal as HHS trying to restore a functioning ACIP amid a quorum vacuum that threatens fall vaccine recommendations, with AAP arguing the government could convene a lawful ACIP at any time.
notes: Tier-2 quality specialist source (University of Minnesota CIDRAP), ~12 June 2026. No on-page dateline captured on fetch; date pinned to the 12 June announcement it reports as news and cross-checked against HPN Online's same-day coverage.

title: RFK Jr. rewrote the ACIP charter. Here's how it changes the committee's responsibilities
date_evidence: URL path /2026/06/25/; corroborated by Medical Daily (30/06/2026): 'According to STAT News detailed reporting, the revised charter redirects the committee's core mission'
key_claim: STAT's reporting on the revised ACIP charter (dated May 14, 2026) finds it redirects the committee's core mission, suggesting the committee should compare vaccines with 'other preventive measures' and advise on 'gaps and limitations in evidence' rather than focus on how to use vaccines effectively and safely, and adds non-voting liaison organisations sceptical of vaccine benefits.
frame_summary: STAT frames the charter rewrite as a substantive reorientation of ACIP's mandate away from optimising vaccine use and toward scrutinising vaccine evidence and harms.
notes: Tier-3 quality journalism (STAT), 25 June 2026. statnews.com is paywalled to the audit fetcher; content and date corroborated by Medical Daily (30/06/2026), which quotes and links the STAT piece directly. Cited for the charter-mission-redirect point.

title: A Rewritten Federal Vaccine Charter Could Determine Whether Your Fall Flu Shot Is Covered by Insurance
date_evidence: meta article:published_time 2026-06-30T18:31:06-04:00; visible 'Published Jun 30, 2026 6:31 PM EDT'
key_claim: ACIP recommendations, once accepted by the CDC director, directly determine which vaccines private insurers must cover without cost-sharing under the ACA, which are bought free for low-income children through VFC, and which Medicare and Medicaid reimburse; with ACIP lacking a functioning quorum since March 2026 there is no finalized fall 2026 respiratory-vaccine recommendation and no clear mechanism to issue one, leaving vaccine-coverage determinations uncertain for roughly 90 million Americans on Medicare, Medicaid or VFC plus privately insured people, even as the CDC invested about $1.24 billion in COVID-19 vaccine contracts in early June 2026 and more than 130 medical organizations objected.
frame_summary: Medical Daily frames the ACIP quorum vacuum as a concrete coverage problem: because no-cost vaccine coverage is legally pegged to ACIP, the absence of a fall 2026 recommendation puts insurance coverage in genuine doubt for tens of millions.
notes: Tier-3 health journalism (Medical Daily / IBT), 30 June 2026. Fetched clean via web_fetch on 2026-07-12, but the site 403-bot-blocks the audit fetcher; manually verified on-page text: 'creating uncertainty for roughly 90 million Americans whose vaccine coverage... depends on that recommendation being finalized'. Load-bearing for the coverage-decoupling mechanism (ACA/VFC/Medicare pegged to ACIP), the ~90 million exposure, the fall-2026 recommendation gap, and the $1.24bn procurement fact. Also corroborates the STAT charter reporting.

publisher: The American Journal of Managed Care
title: AAP Breaks With CDC, Maintains Broader 2026 Childhood and Adolescent Vaccine Schedule
date_evidence: Visible dateline 'News | Articles | January 27, 2026'; references dated 26-27 January 2026
key_claim: The American Academy of Pediatrics released its 2026 schedule recommending protection against 18 diseases versus the CDC's reduced list of 11, and no longer endorses the CDC schedule; twelve other national health organizations and 28 states have endorsed the AAP schedule and will no longer recommend the CDC's, breaking a decades-long collaboration meant to maintain a single set of vaccine guidelines.
frame_summary: AJMC frames the AAP's move as a historic institutional break that ends the decades-long single national immunization standard and establishes a parallel, non-federal recommendation track.
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCHOR (27/01/2026, 3-6m band): the canonical account of the founding structural break (AAP de-endorses the CDC schedule; 18 vs 11 diseases; 28 states + 12 organizations adopt the AAP schedule). Only source outside the 3-month window; the single permitted anchor. (Page meta carries a 2026-07-11 modified timestamp from a CMS refresh; editorial byline is 27 January 2026.)
